messages.subject: problem getting colext to run
parts:
Hi everyone,

I'm trying to fit a multi-year occupancy model. I'm following the
crossbills example in the "Dynamic occupancy models in unmarked"
tutorial written by Marc Kery and Richard Chandler.

I created an unmarkedMultiFrame (summary and structure below), and
then tried to execute the simplest model:

> m1 <- colext(~1, ~1, ~1, ~1, data=umf)

However, the function fails to fully execute. Using "debug," I found
that it's failing around the step:

> fm <- eval(fc)

The message I get is: "Error in .local(umf, ...) : (subscript)
logical subscript too long"

I'm not clear what this step is doing, or why I could be getting this
message.

The "y" data is of monthly surveys spanning 4 years, but they start in
middle of the first year, and end in the middle off the last year. So
the missing months at the beginning and end of those years
respectively are just columns of NA's. But there are a total of 4 x
12 = 48 "y" columns. The site-level and site-year covariates are
all complete. There are not observation covariates in this case.

Any thoughts on what the problem might be would be appreciated.

Erin Kurten

messages.author: 2f4cad6eca9a18e4
messages.subject: Re: problem getting colext to run
parts:
Hi Richard,

If I had understood what the problem was, I might have been better
able to replicate the problem with an example. But after some
experimentation I learned this:

For my"Site Covariates," I'd taken my raw covariates data frame and
created a new set columns of scaled covariates, for the columns in
which I was interested. I then subset this data frame as my argument
for "siteCovs" in the "unmarkedMultFrame" function. As one can note
in the "structure" information for the umf in my original message, the
scaling information seems to carry over into the unmarkedMultFrame.

However, when I created a fresh data frame of those scaled columns and
used that as the argument for "siteCovs" (rather than the original
columns from the original data frame), the scaling information wasn't
carried over to the unmarkedMultFrame. This version seems to run.
Below is the structure of the umf that doesn't get stuck at the "fm
<- eval(fc)" step of colext. You'll notice that the only difference
between this umf, and the umf in my original message is in the
@siteCovs component.

I'm still not clear on why having the scaling attributes present vs.
not would cause the error I encountered, but at least the basic model
seems to be running with that modification.

Best,
Erin
